reason: E1 shows Mo improves room-temperature and elevated-temperature strength in Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys, but these are refractory-based, not Ti-Ni-primary. E2 discusses Ni/Co additions to Al-Nb-Ti-V alloys, not Mo, and focuses on sigma precipitates. Neither passage provides evidence for Mo's effect in a Ti-Ni-primary HEA system, so the key premises about solid-solution strengthening and precipitate formation in this specific context are unsupported.
premises: Mo addition increases room-temperature strength in refractory HEAs
High-melting-point elements like Mo improve elevated-temperature strength in refractory HEAs
Mo can promote solid-solution strengthening and precipitate formation in Ti-containing alloys
The cited evidence is directly transferable to Ti-Ni-primary HEAs
